metadata.title: Seedance 2.5 Reference to Video: Workflow, Limits & Examples
metadata.description: Learn how Seedance 2.5 reference-to-video workflows use images, video, audio, and prompts for controlled motion, identity, editing, and scene continuity.

hero.title: Seedance 2.5 Reference to Video
hero.description: A practical Seedance reference-to-video guide for organizing source assets, labeling references, controlling motion, checking limits, and evaluating the returned clip.
hero.tip: Reference limits and syntax are provider-specific. Check the current API or product documentation before uploading a large asset set.

introduce.title: What reference-to-video means
introduce.description: Reference-to-video uses source material to guide identity, composition, motion, style, audio, or scene structure. The prompt should explain the role of each reference instead of merely listing files.

items.title: Image references
items.description: Use images for characters, products, locations, wardrobe, composition, style, or a first-frame anchor.

items.title: Video references
items.description: Use a clip to guide motion, blocking, camera language, timing, or a visual transformation.

items.title: Audio references
items.description: Use audio for voice, ambience, rhythm, or a sound-led creative direction where the provider supports it.

items.title: Prompt instructions
items.description: State what to preserve, what to change, when the change happens, and how the camera should connect the shots.

benefits.title: Reference-to-video patterns
benefits.description: These patterns cover common searches such as “how do reference images work in Seedance 2.5?” and “change reference video style.”

items.title: Identity lock
items.description: Reference the subject and explicitly preserve face, costume, proportions, colors, and key props while changing the action.

items.title: Motion transfer with intent
items.description: Use a motion clip as a starting point, then specify the new subject, setting, camera, and physical constraints.

items.title: Scene continuity
items.description: Use multiple references for locations, characters, and props, and define the order and spatial relationship in the prompt.

items.title: Controlled edit
items.description: For a background or green-screen change, name the source clip, replacement environment, lighting interaction, and timing.

features.title: A reference-to-video workflow
features.description: Organize references before generation so the result is easier to reproduce and troubleshoot.

items.title: 1. Define the invariant
items.description: Write what must not change: identity, product geometry, camera framing, timing, or audio cue.

items.title: 2. Assign each reference
items.description: Label each image, video, or audio asset by role and avoid ambiguous “use all files” instructions.

items.title: 3. Describe the transformation
items.description: State the new action, environment, style, camera path, and exact time window for the change.

items.title: 4. Check input limits
items.description: Verify count, duration, size, format, aspect ratio, and URL access for the provider and mode.

items.title: 5. Run a small test
items.description: Use fewer references first, then add complexity only when the identity and motion are stable.

items.title: 6. Inspect continuity
items.description: Review the opening, middle, transition, and ending for drift, flicker, broken physics, or mismatched sound.

faq.title: Seedance 2.5 Reference-to-Video FAQ
faq.description: Clear answers for the most common Seedance searches and workflows.

items.question: How do reference images work in Seedance 2.5?
items.answer: They can guide subjects, scenes, composition, style, props, and other visual attributes. Label the role of each image and confirm the provider’s current count and format limits.

items.question: How does a Seedance 2.5 avatar reference video work?
items.answer: Official materials describe reference-video workflows. If you are asking what’s the max length a reference video can be for Seedance 2.5, check the exact provider and endpoint because duration and clip limits vary.

items.question: How can I change a Seedance 2.5 reference video style?
items.answer: For a Seedance 2.5 change reference video style workflow, identify the source video’s motion or blocking and state the intended style or environment change. Preserve only the attributes you actually need.

items.question: How many images can Seedance 2.5 reference?
items.answer: Current official API materials describe expanded image-reference support, including up to 30 images in a supported multimodal workflow. Verify the live endpoint before relying on that limit.

items.question: Can I use first and last frames?
items.answer: Seedance 2 reference-to-video can refer to an older or provider-specific workflow. Some Seedance surfaces expose first-frame and first/last-frame controls; check the exact mode and interface because a provider may implement the capability differently.

items.question: Why does a reference workflow change the person or product?
items.answer: References guide a probabilistic generation. Use clearer identity anchors, fewer simultaneous actions, explicit preservation constraints, and a simpler camera path; always confirm you have rights to the source.

cta.title: Turn references into a controlled shot
cta.description: Start with one clear invariant, label every source asset, and verify the provider’s current reference limits before scaling up.
